title: Can robots that take over from fading allies keep a crowd tipped, and is that cheaper than fielding them upfront?
lede: is a hand-over cheaper than buying robots first? With 20% allies fading at rate c and 10% robots at the start, replacing half of fading allies with robots tips 10 of 12 crowds at c = 0.03 but ends with 0.19 robots, against 0.15 robots upfront in society-allyfade; below 5% initial robots only full replacement tips anything. Stylised
summary: The society-allyfade model (20% allies, memory 9, 200 people, 12 seeds, 2000 rounds) where a fading ally becomes a committed robot with probability h. With 10% robots at the start, h = 0.5 tips 10 of 12 crowds at fade rate c = 0.03 but ends with 0.19 robots, while 0.15 robots bought upfront do the same, so hand-over is dominated by upfront robots; it helps only on the margin (slow fading, h = 0.1 lifts 11 to 12 of 12). At 0 to 2% initial robots only h = 1 tips, ending near the no-ally threshold 0.2165. Stylised: c and h are swept, not measured; instant replacement; simulated walkers only.
